title: Chamthei: A Tangkhul Novel of Highland Trials and Hope
alternate_titles: Chamthei: The Story of Resilience in a Tangkhul Village
subject: Novel (Upanyas), Social Realism & Highland Life
notes: Celebrated realistic Tangkhul novel portraying the generational transformation of a mountain village, documenting jhum cultivation hardships, the advent of schools, and the triumph of integrity over despair.

front_matter.title_page: Chamthei: A Tangkhul Novel of Highland Trials and Hope (1983)
front_matter.preface: Chamthei (literally 'Fruit of Patience/Perseverance') depicts the profound social transformations of 20th-century Tangkhul hill society. Centered around a determined orphan youth who overcomes poverty, superstition, and crop failures through terrace irrigation and education, this novel is widely celebrated for its realistic dialogue and agrarian terminology.

chapters.title: The Hardship of Jhum Cultivation (Luiramli Ot Kasa)
chapters.summary: Depicts slash-and-burn farming on steep slopes, erratic weather, and village cooperative labor (Ngarun).
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 1: Zingkhamathān shoklakha, Chamtheina awui kakhut eina kaphungli thukzatsaye. Ana jhum luiramli thing phunglaga meithei shukserie. Kala awui ava-vana kathi tharan, a kacham thotlaga khikha maleisai; kha ana Ngarun (cooperative labor) eina village-wui yaronaobing eina ot sai. Ana hang: 'Ningkazang eina ngaleili ot sadaran, ngaleina theiwon kaphā mishukra!'
chapters.english_translation: At early dawn, Chamthei climbed the steep mountain slopes with his farming implements. He felled trees and cleared the slope for jhum cultivation. Orphaned since childhood, he possessed no family riches; yet through the traditional Ngarun cooperative system, he labored shoulder-to-shoulder with village youths. He declared: 'If one toils upon the earth with persevering heart, the earth will never withhold its abundant fruit!'
grammar_notes: Agricultural cooperation idiom: 'Ngarun' reflects egalitarian mutual aid.
Proverbial encouragement: earth rewards persevering labor ('ningkazang eina ot').
exercises: Explain the communal function of Ngarun in traditional Tangkhul agriculture.
How does Chamthei overcome his initial poverty?

chapters.title: The Arrival of the New School (Lairik Shim Kathara)
chapters.summary: The arrival of modern primary schooling in the village and Chamthei's passionate thirst for knowledge.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 2: Ukhrul eina tuitamkasana village-li rarlaga lairik shim phokserie. Mikumo charakhana hang: 'Lairik hanglaga kachak phāmacho?' Kha Chamtheina zingsho ngazing kachikhali slate kala chalk khuilaga tuitam khuiye. Ana Roman script eina Tangkhul grammar, English, kala mathematics kaphāmei khuiye. Ana theitserie: Theikakhui china village-li kashilashili eina huikhuira.
chapters.english_translation: A teacher arrived from Ukhrul and established the village's first primary school. Some skeptical elders murmured: 'Can mere book-reading fill a stomach with grain?' Yet Chamthei embraced slate and chalk with relentless dedication day and night. He mastered Tangkhul orthography in Roman script, English vocabulary, and arithmetic. He realized: True knowledge is the sole path to emancipate the village from poverty.
exercises: Why did traditional elders initially question the value of schooling?
Identify Chamthei's academic achievements in Chapter 2.

chapters.title: Harvest of Hope & Village Renaissance (Theiwon Kashung)
chapters.summary: Chamthei introduces terrace canal irrigation to the village, producing bumper harvest and social harmony.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 3: Chamtheina village council (Hangva) ngalemli rarlaga kongkhamathān eina terrace irrigation (Lui canal) sakhavai proposal chitheitserie. Eldersbingna awui ningkazang theilaga green signal miye. Zingkum charakha ngaphalaga, terraced fields-li paddy kashung thotna; village-li haora kasham maleilu-mana. Chamtheili village-na 'Awung-ngashan youth leader' hoda mathat-eina kashakserie.
chapters.english_translation: Chamthei stood before the Hangva village council and presented a blueprint to channel mountain streams into terraced irrigation canals. Impressed by his wisdom and steadfast integrity, the elders approved the project. Within seasons, golden paddy swayed across the terraces, banishing famine from the valley. The community honored Chamthei as an exemplary youth leader of the renaissance.
grammar_notes: Civic presentation discourse: standing before the Hangva court.
Eradication of famine expressed through negative completive: 'maleilu-mana'.
exercises: How did modern knowledge and traditional agrarian work combine in Chamthei's success?
What moral does the novel's title Chamthei convey?

pages.title: Harvest of Hope & Village Renaissance (Theiwon Kashung)
lines: CHAPTER 3: HARVEST OF HOPE & VILLAGE RENAISSANCE (THEIWON KASHUNG)
Summary: Chamthei introduces terrace canal irrigation to the village, producing bumper ha...
Chapter 3: Chamtheina village council (Hangva) ngalemli rarlaga
kongkhamathān eina terrace irrigation (Lui canal) sakhavai proposal
chitheitserie. Eldersbingna awui ningkazang theilaga green signal miye.
Zingkum charakha ngaphalaga, terraced fields-li paddy kashung thotna;
village-li haora kasham maleilu-mana. Chamtheili village-na 'Awung-
ngashan youth leader' hoda mathat-eina kashakserie.
Chamthei stood before the Hangva village council and presented a
blueprint to channel mountain streams into terraced irrigation canals.
Impressed by his wisdom and steadfast integrity, the elders approved the
project. Within seasons, golden paddy swayed across the terraces,
banishing famine from the valley. The community honored Chamthei as an
exemplary youth leader of the renaissance.
